newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks soft, seen mixed to steady.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks soft, seen mixed to steady.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks traded softer in an active market on Monday with brokers saying most market players were now waiting for direction from some corporate results due in May.
The dealers however said they expected the market to trade mixed to steady in the next few days as underlying sentiment was still firm.

The key industrial index lost 15.58 points to 10,948.96, pulled down largely by construction and plastics investor IHL which dropped 100 cents to 2,100, merchant banker NMB and hotel and supermarket group Meikles 's 50-cent losses each to 3,450 and 2,900 respectively.
"I think people are just waiting for good corporate results to filter in. While there were some good volumes today, the market is looking soft," one broker said.

Also among the day's losers, pharmaceutical firm Caps shed 50 cents to 1,750, tobacco company TSL lost 20 cents to 680 while clothing retailer Truworths at 1,010 and tyre manufacturer Dunlop at 145 both traded 15 cents off.
Against the trend, timber producer Border leapt 200 cents to 1,550, finance house Finhold rose 45 cents to 750 and cement company Circle gained 30 cents to 780.
Minings remained dull, trapped by lacklustre metals prices and no reporting news except for Wankie Colliery which added 20 cents to 550. The mining index put on 7.27 points to 1,022.15.
